mainTopic: Items too important to be canceled in a mixture: רבי מאיר's 'usually counted' rule, the את/כל wording dispute, and the ברייתא about a single impure holy piece
overview: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת ערלה about a forbidden item that got mixed into permitted food. רבי מאיר says anything usually sold by count is too important to be canceled (בטל), so the whole mixture must be burned. חכמים say only six specific items are that important, and רבי עקיבא adds a seventh: a homeowner's loaves. Next, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about the exact wording of רבי מאיר's rule. 'את' would mean only things that are always counted, while 'כל' would include things that are sometimes counted. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא about an impure piece of a חטאת or of לחם הפנים mixed into a hundred pure pieces. The תנא קמא says it is canceled and רבי יהודה says it is not, but everyone agrees that a pure holy piece mixed into plain pieces is not canceled. The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש from the first half, and רבי חייא בריה דרב הונא answers that the piece was crushed. The גמרא then asks what רבי יהודה's reason could be, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The whole mixture must be burned, or canceled at one in two hundred
steps.stepSummary: The end of a quoted משנה: רבי מאיר says the entire mixture is burned, while חכמים say the forbidden item is canceled when there is one part forbidden to two hundred parts permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They must all be burned. That is רבי מאיר's view. חכמים say they are canceled in a mixture of one to two hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the end of a משנה (from מסכת ערלה) where רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about a mixture that contains forbidden produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says no amount of permitted food can cancel the forbidden item, so everything is burned. חכמים say the normal rule for ערלה and כלאי הכרם applies: if the permitted food is two hundred times as much as the forbidden food, the forbidden part is canceled.

keyTerms.meaning: They must be burned (the item is fully forbidden to use)
Literally 'they go up'; it means they are canceled (בטל) in the mixture
One in two hundred: the ratio needed to cancel ערלה or כלאי הכרם

phrases.english: They must all be burned; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: This picks up in the middle of a משנה. 'All of them' means the whole mixed-up batch, forbidden and permitted together.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
They are nullified in one to two hundred.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the whole mixture is burned. חכמים: the forbidden item is canceled at a ratio of one to two hundred.

steps.title: The principle behind the argument: items that are usually counted
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that anything usually sold by count makes the whole mixture forbidden. חכמים say only six items do this, and רבי עקיבא says seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר used to say: anything that is usually counted makes the mixture forbidden. חכמים say only six items do. רבי עקיבא says seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the reason for רבי מאיר's strict ruling and shows how חכמים and רבי עקיבא narrow it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Items sold one by one, instead of by weight, are treated as important, and an important item is never canceled. רבי מאיר applies this to every such item. חכמים limit it to a fixed list of six, and רבי עקיבא's list has seven.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that is usually counted, meaning sold by the unit
Literally 'sanctifies'; here it means it makes the whole mixture forbidden
Six items: the fixed list according to חכמים

steps.whyThisMatters: This 'usually counted' idea, the concept of an item that is too important to be canceled, is what the rest of this section turns on.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Meir would say:
Anything that is usually counted renders the mixture forbidden.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מְקַדֵּשׁ אֶלָּא שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: Only six items alone render it forbidden.
Rabbi Akiva says: Seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the argument in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: any item usually counted is never canceled. חכמים: only six items. רבי עקיבא: seven.

steps.title: The list of the important items
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the six items: פרך nuts, בדן pomegranates, sealed barrels, beet shoots, cabbage stalks and Greek gourd. רבי עקיבא adds a homeowner's loaves. Each item makes the mixture forbidden under the prohibition that fits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the items: פרך nuts, בדן pomegranates, sealed barrels, beet shoots, cabbage stalks and Greek gourd. רבי עקיבא also adds a homeowner's loaves. The items that can be ערלה make the mixture ערלה, and the items that can be כלאי הכרם make it כלאי הכרם.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה names the exact items on the list from step 2 and tells us which prohibition each one belongs to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These items are all high-quality, so they count as important. The nuts and pomegranates grow on trees, so they can be ערלה. The vegetables can be כלאי הכרם. The mixture takes on whichever prohibition fits the item.

keyTerms.meaning: High-quality nuts from a place called פרך
Pomegranates from a place called בדן
A homeowner's loaves (large, home-baked loaves)
Fruit from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden
Food crops planted in a vineyard, which are forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: חכמים don't use a general 'counted' rule. They give a fixed list of six, and רבי עקיבא adds a seventh.

phrases.english: These are they: Perekh nuts,
and Badan pomegranates, and sealed barrels,
and shoots of beet, and cabbage stalks,
and Greek gourd.
And Rabbi Akiva adds
also a homeowner's loaves.
Those fit for orla render it orla.
phrases.notes: The nuts and pomegranates grow on trees, so these are the ones that can be ערלה.

phrases.english: Those fit for food crops in a vineyard render it food crops in a vineyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the six (or seven) items mentioned in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The six items, plus a homeowner's loaves according to רבי עקיבא, are never canceled. They make the mixture forbidden as ערלה or as כלאי הכרם.

steps.title: Did the משנה say 'that which' or 'anything'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads רבי מאיר's rule as 'את שדרכו לימנות' (that which is usually counted). ריש לקיש reads it as 'כל שדרכו לימנות' (anything usually counted).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן holds that we learned 'that which is usually counted'. ריש לקיש holds that we learned 'anything that is usually counted'.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about the exact wording of רבי מאיר's rule in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one-word difference changes how wide the rule is. 'את' (that which) sounds narrow: only items that are always sold by count. 'כל' (anything) sounds broad: even items that are only sometimes counted are included and can't be canceled.

keyTerms.meaning: That which: a narrower wording
Anything: a broader wording
We learned (in the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not just a fight over spelling. Each wording leads to a different range of items that can never be canceled.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan holds:
We learned: 'That which is usually counted.'
And Reish Lakish holds:
We learned: 'Anything that is usually counted.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סָבַר: ״אֶת שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לִימָּנוֹת״ שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי מאיר's rule from step 2 and argues about its exact wording
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: 'את', the narrow reading. ריש לקיש: 'כל', the broad reading.

steps.title: What case of 'a piece' is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case of a 'piece' (חתיכה) is being talked about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'a piece'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a quick clarifying question to set up the next move: which case of a 'piece' is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא refers to a 'piece' (חתיכה) as a known case connected to the 'usually counted' argument and asks which case it is. The answer comes from a ברייתא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? (a question word)
A piece (of meat)

phrases.english: What is 'a piece'?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific case of a 'piece' (חתיכה) is meant

steps.title: An impure piece of a חטאת or of לחם הפנים in a mixture
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if an impure piece of a חטאת, or an impure slice of לחם הפנים, gets mixed into a hundred pure pieces, the תנא קמא says it is canceled and רבי יהודה says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: an impure piece of a חטאת mixed into a hundred pure pieces of חטאות, and likewise an impure slice of לחם הפנים mixed into a hundred pure slices, is canceled. רבי יהודה says it is not canceled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא about one impure piece of holy food mixed into many pure pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the impure piece is canceled when it is outnumbered a hundred to one. רבי יהודה says it is not canceled, but the ברייתא does not give his reason. The גמרא will use this ברייתא to test the 'usually counted' rule, and step 10 asks directly for רבי יהודה's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
A sin-offering
The showbread placed on the שולחן in the מקדש
It is canceled (in the mixture)
Ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: The 'hundred pieces' here describes the case in the ברייתא. It is not a new canceling ratio to set against the 'one in two hundred' for ערלה and כלאי הכרם in step 1.

phrases.english: As it is taught: a piece of an impure sin-offering
that became mixed into one hundred pieces
of pure sin-offerings,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן פְּרוּסָה שֶׁל לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים טְמֵאָה
phrases.english: and similarly an impure slice of shewbread
that became mixed into one hundred slices
of pure shewbread: it is nullified.
Rabbi Yehuda says: It is not nullified.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'piece' is the case in the ברייתא: an impure piece of a חטאת or of לחם הפנים mixed into a hundred pure pieces. The תנא קמא says it is canceled. רבי יהודה says it is not.

steps.title: The ברייתא's ending: a pure holy piece is never canceled
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. If a pure piece of a חטאת, or a pure slice of לחם הפנים, gets mixed into a hundred pure plain pieces, everyone agrees it is not canceled.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if a pure piece of a חטאת got mixed into a hundred pure pieces of plain meat, or a pure slice of לחם הפנים got mixed into a hundred pure plain slices, everyone agrees it is not canceled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא from Step 6. This is its second half, where the holy piece is pure instead of impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6 the holy piece was impure, and there the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה argued. Here the holy piece is pure, and now there is no argument: everyone says it is not canceled. This sets up a contrast between the two halves of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Plain food that is not holy
Everyone agrees
It is not canceled (literally, 'it does not go up')
A slice (of bread)

phrases.english: But a pure piece of a sin-offering
that got mixed into a hundred pieces
of pure, non-holy meat,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן פְּרוּסָה שֶׁל לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים טְהוֹרָה
phrases.english: and likewise a pure slice of the showbread
that got mixed into a hundred slices
of pure, non-holy bread —
everyone agrees it is not canceled.
phrases.notes: Compare with Step 6, where the holy piece was impure and there was an argument. Here it is pure, so everyone agrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 6 with its second clause.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא's second clause: a pure holy piece mixed into a hundred plain pieces is not canceled, according to everyone.

steps.title: The first half of the ברייתא says the impure piece is canceled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the first half of the ברייתא says the impure holy piece is canceled. That seems to go against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the first part of the ברייתא teaches that it is canceled!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש. He says anything usually counted cannot be canceled, yet the ברייתא says an impure piece of meat, which can be counted, is canceled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא in the first half, the impure piece of חטאת is canceled in a hundred. A piece of meat is sometimes sold by count, so by ריש לקיש's wide reading ('כל שדרכו לימנות') it should not be canceled. For רבי יוחנן, who limits the rule to items that are always sold by count, there is no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches
In any case, at least
The first part of a teaching

phrases.english: In any case, the first part teaches
phrases.notes: The 'first part' is the case in Step 6, where the holy piece was impure.

phrases.english: it is canceled!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the first clause of the ברייתא just quoted to attack ריש לקיש's position from Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reading that anything usually counted (כל שדרכו לימנות) is never canceled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A piece of holy meat is something people count, yet the תנא קמא says the impure piece is canceled in a hundred. That goes against ריש לקיש's wide rule.

steps.title: The piece had been crushed
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בריה דרב הונא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a piece that was crushed, so it is no longer a whole countable piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא, the son of רב הונא, said: it is talking about a piece that was crushed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בריה דרב הונא defends ריש לקיש by saying the ברייתא is talking about a crushed piece.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A crushed piece is not a whole piece anymore, so it is no longer something people count. That is why it can be canceled, and ריש לקיש's rule about counted things does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: About one that was crushed or broken apart
The son of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya, son of Rav Huna, said:
It is talking about one that was crushed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא בְּנִימּוֹחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against ריש לקיש by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about a crushed piece
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא meant a whole piece of meat, which is counted, so canceling it would go against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The piece was crushed, so it is not counted, and canceling it fits ריש לקיש.

steps.title: Then why does רבי יהודה say it is not canceled?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the piece was crushed, what reason does רבי יהודה have for saying it is not canceled?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 9. If the piece is crushed and not counted, why would רבי יהודה say it is not canceled?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the piece is crushed, the counting reason is gone. So רבי יהודה's view in Step 6, that it is not canceled, now needs a different explanation. The גמרא is setting up its next move: finding רבי יהודה's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
What is the reason?

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if the piece was really crushed, as Step 9 just said.

phrases.english: what is Rabbi Yehuda's reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 9 by asking how רבי יהודה's view in the ברייתא still makes sense.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא בריה דרב הונא's claim that the ברייתא is about a crushed piece
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A crushed piece is not counted, so there seems to be no reason left for רבי יהודה to say it is not canceled.
